subject: Sandbox vs VPC evaluation: proposed plan & success agreement
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@carenova.com>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@carenova.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-14T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call summary + hosting options for CareNova evaluation

Hi Elena / Tom —

Great to meet you both on the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed path forward so we can lock the POC schedule this week. High level notes:

- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for CareNova triage assistant (redaction + PHI-safe routing) and measure latency/cost at typical load.
- Primary constraint: security/regulatory — anything involving PHI will need either private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or strict data controls in Dedicated.
- Technical ask from your side: target throughput (concurrent inference rate), representative prompt set, and test dataset for quality checks.

Options we proposed:
1) Hosted API (fastest to start) — best for UX & iteration but not acceptable if PHI is in the payload.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity in our infra) — isolated capacity, short lead time (~3–5 business days) and allows logs/audit controls; good middle ground.
3) Private VPC (customer-managed network) — highest compliance posture, longer lead time (2–4 weeks depending on networking/KMS).

Proposed experiment plan (two-track approach we recommend):
- Week 0: Kickoff and environment decision (you confirm preferred path).
- Weeks 1–2: If you pick Dedicated, we stand up the sandbox and ingest sample prompts; if you pick VPC, we start the network onboarding tasks in parallel (so VPC can go live by Week 3–4).
- Weeks 3–4: Steady-state run: run 1000 representative chats/day, measure latency, accuracy, and token cost.

Suggested success criteria (please review):
- Functional: model outputs pass the 90% acceptance rate on labeled prompt set (per your QA rubric).
- Performance: p50 latency < 200ms; p95 latency < 650ms at 20 concurrent requests.
- Economics: unit cost below your target (we estimate ~$X per 1k tokens for this config; we'll firm this up after we see the trace).
- Ops: audit logs available, RBAC set up, and runbook for failover to an alternate model.

Attachments: I attached a short POC checklist and a template for VPC requirements to make the decision easier.

Ask / next steps:
1) Confirm if PHI will be included in test payloads (yes/no).
2) Which hosting path do you want us to prioritize (Dedicated sandbox or VPC)? If neither, we can start with Hosted for non-PHI data.
3) Share the sample prompt set and preferred 2-hour window for the kickoff next week.

I'll wait for your confirmation and will draft a short mutual success agreement once you confirm the path.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (summary checklist), vpc-requirements-template.xlsx (network fields)
From: Elena Martinez <elena@carenova.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@carenova.com>
Date: 2028-02-14T17:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call summary + hosting options for CareNova evaluation

Thanks Ben — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Yes, our initial test set will include redacted PHI and some live transcripts with identifiers removed. We cannot send raw PHI to a public hosted API.
- Preference: we would like the final POC to run in a VPC or a dedicated environment where logs and audit are retained in our tenancy. That said, if Dedicated sandbox gets us to results faster, we can run an early functional pass there provided logs are segregated and access controls are enforced.
- Throughput: target 25 concurrent inference requests during peak test periods; baseline for acceptance is stable p95 under 800ms.
- Timeline: we're aiming to present results to the CIO on March 12 — ideally a 3-week POC window.

Questions:
1) For Dedicated sandbox, what exact RBAC/audit controls can be enabled? Can we restrict token-level access to a named admin?
2) For VPC, can you share a sample network diagram and the typical firewall rules we need to open?

Tom, can you confirm whether CareNova security will be able to start the firewall change window next week?

Elena
Elena Martinez
Head of AI, CareNova Health
---
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@carenova.com>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@carenova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call summary + hosting options for CareNova evaluation

Hi Elena / Tom — looping in Ops checklist and a proposed runbook excerpt so you can see the minimal items for each hosting option. I attached the checklist and a VPC template. Quick answers to your questions:

- Dedicated sandbox RBAC: yes — we can provision tenant-scoped API keys and restrict access to named accounts; audit logs (request metadata, timestamps, model version) are retained per your retention policy. We can also enable read-only views for your auditors.
- VPC networking: see vpc-requirements-template.xlsx attached — we need a small set of outbound firewall rules to Redwood egress IPs, a TLS-terminated endpoint, and an optional KMS integration for key wrapping. The typical change window we ask for is 2–4 hours for initial validation.

Proposed compromise path (recommended):
- Start with Dedicated sandbox (we can stand up in 3 business days after we receive the sample prompt set and an account admin).
- Parallel VPC readiness: CareNova begins network/infra prep immediately; Redwood provides the network diagram and preflight checklist within 24 business hours.

Operational items we need from CareNova to start (minimal):
1) Name & email of two sandbox admins.
2) Representative prompt set and 50 initial evaluation prompts with expected labels.
3) Target peak concurrency window (25 concurrent requests confirmed).
4) Contact for networking changes and a preferred window (Tom — can you confirm?).

If that sounds OK I'll schedule the kickoff and provision the sandbox.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf, vpc-requirements-template.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@carenova.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@carenova.com>
Date: 2028-02-16T11:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sandbox vs VPC evaluation: proposed plan & success agreement

Elena / Tom — thanks for the quick replies and for confirming constraints. Based on Monica's notes I'll draft a short Mutual Success Agreement (MSA) that summarizes the acceptance criteria, timelines, and owner list. Key highlights to expect in the MSA:

- Acceptance tests: 100 labeled prompts (we'll run daily batches) with a pass threshold of >=90% acceptance; end-to-end regression tests for NER redaction.
- Performance SLA targets (as negotiated): p50 < 200ms, p95 < 650ms at 25 concurrent reqs; if we exceed p95 > 1s consistently we commit to a follow-up tuning pass.
- Data handling: Logs retained for 90 days by default in Dedicated; in VPC we can mirror logs to your storage with your KMS.
- Rollout plan: Week 0 -> kickoff; Days 1–3 sandbox standup (Dedicated); Days 4–10 iteration and baseline runs; Weeks 2–3 steady-state validation and dashboards.

I'll also estimate costs for both configurations once Monica confirms expected daily token volumes; that will let us propose a ballpark budget you can review before the CIO briefing.

Proposed kickoff slots:
- Wed 2028-02-21 09:00–10:00 PST
- Thu 2028-02-22 14:00–15:00 PST

Please tell me which works and we'll lock it.

Best —
Ben
